input.quote: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: No convenience-termination right exists anywhere in the Agreement: Section 9 contains only cause-based exits (9.1 material breach, 9.2 insolvency, 9.3 Customer's immediate rights for security/SLA/law/IP), 9.5 is a non-cross-termination rule, and searches for "for convenience", "without cause" and "early termination fee" return nothing. The only unwind is non-renewal at the end of an Order Form term under 8.2, while 8.1 fixes a three-year term and 2.1 states the take-or-pay commitment is "without reduction or termination rights". Absence of a Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is walk-away territory under this rule, so fallback cannot be met on its material terms. We therefore insert a new 9.4 at the preferred level: Customer convenience termination of the Agreement or any Order Form on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and no Vendor convenience right during a committed term. Section 10.2 already requires refund of prepaid recurring Fees for the post-termination period, so the new clause is consistent with the existing refund mechanic; the take-or-pay volume commitment itself is left to the minimum-commitment rule, and 9.4 opens with a Section 2.1 override only so the exit right is operative. Vendor gains no convenience right, so no counterparty benefit is being disturbed.

proposal.summary: Insert a new Section 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience termination right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and barring Vendor convenience termination during a committed term.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 9 provides only cause-based exits under a three-year term, so we have inserted a 9.4 convenience right (overriding Section 2.1's "no termination rights" language) on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and confirmed Vendor may not exit a committed term for convenience. If 30 days is difficult we can move to 60–90 days' notice with any early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees.

ops.text: Notwithstanding Section 2.1, Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, on thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees pro rata for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
